conviction_note: The findings sum to +1.8: a ~10% sell-off since 12 Nov with no company news, two straight quarters of beating the company's own guide (stock +9.7% and +7.5%), and a mall landlord reporting faster traffic. Against them sit a strong put skew (+8.82 vol pts), weak store traffic and the -24.8% reaction to last year's Q3 guide cut. abs_move 11.5 (the 11.02 event-implied move, nudged up because the Q4 holiday guide is in play) x p_up 54 gives +0.92. That is smaller than the sum because the skew and the next-guide risk pull p_up toward 50; the sum itself was left unscaled.

So the street sits at the TOP of the company's guide on both lines. Benzinga's $0.27 EPS figure is stale and was rejected. Sized against revenue ~$1.545B and adjusted EPS $0.11-0.12.

After the ~10% pre-print slide, an in-line quarter with a held guide probably clears it.

next_guide.street_next_quarter: Not found directly. Implied Q4 street adjusted EPS is ~$1.57-1.62 if the FY street of $2.63 holds and Q3 prints $0.11-0.12 (Q1 $0.32 + Q2 $0.62 already reported).
next_guide.street_full_year: Adjusted EPS $2.63 on revenue $7.11B (Earnings Whispers, at the Q2 print, https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/BBWI). Not re-verified since.
next_guide.company_current_guide: FY2026 adjusted EPS $2.60-2.80, GAAP $3.13-3.33, net sales down 4% to 2.5% (from $7,291M), FCF ~$650M, no buybacks assumed, capex $240M (8-K ex-99.1, 2026-08-26). Implied Q4 adjusted EPS is ~$1.54-1.79 against $2.00 in Q4 FY25.
next_guide.basis: The street ($2.63) already sits near the bottom of the company's FY range, so holding the range, or narrowing it to its lower half, is not a cut against the street. The risk is a holiday read like last year's, when the Q3 FY25 print cut the outlook and the stock fell 24.8%. The 10-Q flags $35M of extra marketing and ~$30M of second-half tariff and input cost pressure, and the CEO said 'underlying business trends remain pressured'.

findings.finding: BBWI fell about 10% from the 12 Nov close of $21.08 to $18.925 (and 12.9% over 5 days) into the print, including -9.9% on 16 Nov, with no company release or guidance change. The pre-print bar is therefore lower than the consensus at the top of the guide implies.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline: the last three prints rose (+2.6, +9.7, +7.5); Q3 FY25 fell 24.8% on a guide cut. Run-up before those prints is not in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: The slide is the price itself, so the question is whether it overshoots. If the market had only re-priced risk, implied vol and skew would be elevated but the stock would not be 10% lower on no news. The event straddle (11.6%) is near the name's tail history, so a held guide has room to recover part of the slide. The skew (+8.82) says the market still fears the downside tail, which is why this is sized small.
findings.independence: StockStory (2026-11-18): -6.3% over the month against +2.7% for specialty-retail peers (https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nyse/bbwi/news/earnings/bath-and-body-works-q3-earnings-report-preview-what-to-look-for). The 12 Nov close comes from the TradingView UBS item.

findings.finding: The company has beaten its own guide two quarters running: Q1 adjusted EPS $0.32 against the $0.29 street, and Q2 ex-refund $0.31 against a $0.20-0.25 guide on revenue of $1.514B against $1.50B. The Q3 guide of $0.07-0.12 on $1.514-1.554B looks set to the same conservative pattern, though the street sits at its top ($0.11-0.12, $1.54-1.55B).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide beats in Q1 and Q2 2026 were bought (+9.7% and +7.5%), and Q4 FY25 +2.6%. Q3 FY25 missed and cut, -24.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: The street already sits at the top of the guide, so an ordinary beat is partly expected. What is not priced after the slide is that a beat repeats. If it were priced, the stock would not be trading 10% below its 12 Nov level into a print whose guide the company has beaten twice.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers Q2 page (consensus $0.24 against $0.62 reported, https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/BBWI) and the Q1 release (https://investors.bbwinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/bath-body-works-reports-first-quarter-results-exceeding-guidance). These are different documents for different quarters.

findings.finding: Simon Property Group, BBWI's largest mall landlord type, reported on 5 Nov that shopper traffic growth 'accelerated for the third consecutive quarter'. Retailer sales were $852/sq ft TTM to 30 Sep 2026, +14.8% y/y, and occupancy 96.5%. That covers most of BBWI's fiscal Q3 (Aug-Oct).
findings.link: BBWI is a mall tenant. Company-operated stores were 1,937 at 2026-08-01 (10-Q). The share of those in Simon or other enclosed malls was not sourced. Simon's quarter ends 30 Sep; BBWI's Q3 ends ~31 Oct.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: BBWI's Q2 store sales were -5.4% on weak traffic while malls were strong, so mall traffic has not transmitted to BBWI's store line before.
findings.why_not_priced: Simon spoke after BBWI's 26 Aug guide and BBWI has not updated since. Previews quote only Q2's -5.4% store decline. If priced, previews would cite mall-traffic acceleration as upside to the store line; none found does.
findings.independence: Proxy: a landlord's aggregate, not BBWI's number. The NRF Retail Monitor (Oct +3.57% y/y but slowing) is a separate, weaker series.

findings.finding: The CNBC/NRF Retail Monitor put October 2026 US retail sales at +3.57% y/y and +0.15% m/m, the 13th straight gain, with growth slowing on higher petrol prices and consumers seeking promotions.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None; macro has not been the line BBWI traded on.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public macro data, so likely priced. It is filed because it points both ways: volume is positive, but the promotion-seeking cuts against BBWI's gross margin.
findings.independence: Proxy. Simon's traffic comment points the same way on volume.

findings.finding: The next guide is the swing. The FY adjusted EPS guide of $2.60-2.80 implies Q4 adjusted EPS of ~$1.54-1.79 against $2.00 last year. The street FY of $2.63 already sits near the bottom of that range, so maintaining or narrowing to the lower half is not a cut against the street. The 10-Q flags extra marketing, ~$30M of H2 tariff and input cost pressure, and no buybacks in the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY25 guide cut: -24.8%. Q2 2026 FY raise: +7.5%. Q1 2026 reaffirm: +9.7%.
findings.why_not_priced: The +8.82 put skew and the 10% slide suggest the market is pricing a holiday cut. If the street already expected a cut below $2.60, its FY would sit below the range rather than at $2.63. The gap between the options' fear and the street's number is the unpriced part, in either direction.
findings.independence: The company 8-K ex-99.1 (FY guide) and the 10-Q (marketing, no buyback) share the 26 Aug filing date. The street number has one source and was not re-verified for November.

findings.finding: Store sales remain the weak line: Q2 US and Canada store sales -5.4% on weak traffic. The Q3 guide (-5% to -2.5%) implies no improvement, and the CEO said 'underlying business trends remain pressured', while ~$35M of extra marketing is being tested against ~$30M of H2 tariff and input costs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Store weakness was in the Q2 print and the stock still rose 7.5%. In Q3 FY25 weak sales plus a cut gave -24.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is the reason the guide is low. It is filed because a sales print at the bottom of the guide ($1.514B) would miss a street that sits at the top.
findings.independence: The Q2 8-K CEO quote is a different document but the same underlying fact. Net of the rest of the company: direct sales +3% and international +24.9% in Q2, so stores (~80% of sales) decide it.

findings.finding: The 25-delta skew is +8.82 vol points and the event-implied move 11.0%, so the options market pays for a downside tail. Short interest is only ~8.7% of float with 2.6 days to cover, so no squeeze mechanism offsets a negative surprise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The name's tail is to the downside: -24.8% and -12.7% in the last eight prints, against a maximum of +9.7% up.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price's own statement, filed so the judges weigh the skew explicitly. The long findings above cut against it.
findings.independence: The sealed baseline's option chain (skew, P/C OI 0.41) is separate from the short-interest pages.

findings.finding: Analysts lifted targets during the quarter: UBS raised to $22 from $17 (Neutral) on ~13 Nov, and Wells Fargo holds $25 Overweight (29 Oct). The mean target of $22.5-24.9 sits 16-24% above the $18.93 spot after the slide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell 6.7% the session after the UBS raise, so target moves have not supported the price.
findings.why_not_priced: Public and in the wire, so mostly priced. The point is that sell-side direction was up while the stock fell, which marks the slide as positioning rather than an estimate cut.
findings.independence: TradingView UBS item and Quiver's target list (Wells Fargo $25 on 10/29). The same broker actions are reported on several sites.

findings.finding: The 10-Q says the ~$85M of IEEPA refunds received in Q2 is 'the significant majority of refunds the Company expects to receive', so any residual refund recognised in Q3 would be small and is not in the Q3 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The $80M Q2 refund print was bought (+7.5%), but the ex-refund beat carried the quality story.
findings.why_not_priced: Any residual is unquantified and the market will look through it. Sized at a fraction because it has no path into the guide.

findings.finding: Capital: no buybacks YTD and none assumed in the FY guide. $117M of authorisation remains, and FCF is guided at ~$650M. After Q2 ended the company redeemed $250M of 2029 notes, so cash went to deleveraging (total debt $3.61B). A restarted buyback would be an upside option on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No capital-return surprise in the last eight prints to compare.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody previews a buyback because none is guided. If the market expected one, the 10% slide would be odd for a name with ~16% of its market cap in annual FCF. This is also a financing item: the money went to debt paydown, which is a neutral-to-positive answer.
findings.independence: Same 10-Q as the refund finding (one document, different lines).

findings.finding: Insider and governance: on 21 Sep the CEO received a $10M PSU with stock-price hurdles of $40-$100 (8-K 2026-09-23). Interim CFO Javitch got a one-time RSU grant on 10 Nov (Form 4, 2026-11-12), and no permanent CFO has been named since June. No open-market insider buys or sells of size were found.
findings.why_not_priced: Not an earnings driver. Filed for completeness: the interim CFO's retention grant days before the print hints that a permanent CFO is not about to be named.
findings.independence: Form 4 doc4.xml (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/701985/000122520826008887/doc4.xml) is a separate filing.

outside_window.finding: Holiday-quarter (Q4) performance, Candle Day in early December and the result of the creator-led holiday campaign land in the Q4 print (~March 2027). Only the guide for it lands in this window.
The search for a permanent CFO has been open since 26 May 2026 (8-K), and its timing is unknown.

baseline_tension: The findings lean long (a sell-off on no news, a guide-beat record, mall traffic), which cuts against the +8.82 put skew. The 12.9% 5-day drop agrees with the skew on fear but partly spends it, so p_up stays only slightly above 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (sign against a strong skew): the sell-off/expectations finding cut from +1.5 to +1.0, and p_up from 56 to 54.
Lesson 5 (proxy is smaller, 'no news' drawdown is not a cause): Simon counterparty cut from +0.5 to +0.4; the drawdown finding kept only as a lower bar, not as evidence of mispricing.
Lesson 2 (one-offs at a fraction): residual tariff refund cut from +0.2 to +0.1.
Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the bar is sourced to the company guide plus two roughly agreeing street sources, so no cap; the stale $0.27 consensus stays rejected.
Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction): the guide-beat finding left at +1.0, because this name's guide beats were bought in Q1 and Q2 2026.
